newsitem.title: DUBAI: Dissident held in Canada prefers trial in Saudi.
newsitem.headline: Dissident held in Canada prefers trial in Saudi.

text.p: A Saudi Arabian dissident held in Canada for his alleged role in a blast that killed 19 U.S. airmen in the kingdom in June was on Thursday quoted as saying he preferred to stand trial in Saudi Arabia.

Hani Abdel-Rahim Hussein al-Sayegh, a 28-year-old Shi'ite Moslem, said he wanted to stand trial in his country if he was given the choice and assured of what he called "international guarantees", the Saudi-owned Al-Hayat newspaper said.
The London-based paper Sayegh was speaking in a telephone interview from his Ottawa prison on Wednesday.

"He said he prefers to stand (trial)...in Saudi if he was given the choice. He said one of the reasons was being close to his family," al-Hayat said. "He said he would be willing to go to Saudi immediately if he is guaranteed a public trial with international guarantees."

Al-Hayat quoted Sayegh as saying he had decided to change his lawyer and appoint the lawyer who represented another Saudi, Fahad al-Shehri, held in the same prison on charges of terrorism unrelated to the bombing. Shehri denies the charges.
Sayegh was arrested in Ottawa on March 18 on the grounds that he posed a security threat to Canada.
Saudi Arabia has made no comment on his arrest and would not confirm press reports that it had asked for his extradition.
The Canadian government has charged that Sayegh was a driver involved in the truck bomb in the eastern city of al-Khobar.

Sayegh denies any role in the bombing and has said he was in Syria last June. He arrived in Canada applying for refugee status from Saudi Arabia because of what he said was the way the Sunni Moslem government treated Shi'ites.
